items.title: USN-8993-1: SOGo vulnerability
items.summary:
It was discovered that SOGo used the client-supplied Origin header when
constructing password reset links. A remote attacker could possibly use
this issue to obtain password reset tokens and take over user accounts.

items.title: USN-8992-1: Shapelib vulnerability
items.summary:
It was discovered that the shpsort utility in Shapelib incorrectly handled
certain inputs, leading to a double free. An attacker could possibly use
this issue to cause a denial of service, or possibly execute arbitrary
code.

items.title: USN-8991-1: rxvt-unicode vulnerability
items.summary:
It was discovered that rxvt-unicode incorrectly handled certain escape
sequences. An attacker could possibly use this issue to execute arbitrary
code if a user displayed specially crafted text in the terminal.

items.title: USN-8990-1: Sprockets vulnerability
items.summary:
It was discovered that Sprockets incorrectly handled certain specially
crafted requests when the Sprockets server was used in production. A remote
attacker could possibly use this issue to access files outside of the
application's root directory.

items.title: USN-8988-1: Relax-and-Recover vulnerability
items.summary:
It was discovered that Relax-and-Recover created a world-readable initrd
when GRUB_RESCUE was enabled. A local attacker could possibly use this
issue to obtain sensitive information.

items.title: USN-8986-1: Swift Mailer vulnerability
items.summary:
Dawid Golunski discovered that Swift Mailer did not properly sanitize
e-mail addresses in the mail transport. A remote attacker could possibly
use this issue to pass extra parameters to the mail command and execute
arbitrary code.

items.title: USN-8985-1: Net::EasyTCP vulnerability
items.summary:
It was discovered that Net::EasyTCP used the built-in Perl rand() function
to generate encryption keys when no strong randomization module was
present. An attacker could possibly use this issue to predict the keys and
obtain sensitive information.

items.title: USN-8984-1: jabberd2 vulnerability
items.summary:
It was discovered that jabberd2 allowed SASL ANONYMOUS authentication even
when it was not enabled in the configuration. A remote attacker could
possibly use this issue to bypass authentication.
